text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: The Kivaro District Community Health Initiative, launched in March 2021 by Hope Meridian Trust, has trained 412 community health workers across nine sub-counties. In each sub-county, health workers mentored village volunteers on recognising danger signs in newborns. At mid-term, household visit coverage reached 68 percent of targeted homes, up from a baseline of 31 percent. Workers reported that monthly supervision visits improved their confidence in screening children for malnutrition. However, stock-outs of oral rehydration salts were common, and supplies did not arrive in Lumbe sub-county for three consecutive quarters. Referral completion rates rose to 54 percent, although the evaluation team could not verify records from two remote health posts. Stipends were paid on time in most months, but no worker received the promised bicycle allowance during the first year.

passages.source_passage: Smallholder farmers in the Orsana Plateau have faced four failed rainy seasons since 2018, and average sorghum yields have fallen by 37 percent over the same period. Most households still plant long-maturing maize varieties that cannot survive dry spells longer than three weeks. Between 2020 and 2022, the Greenfold Cooperative Alliance distributed drought-tolerant millet seed to 1,200 farmers in a small pilot. Participating farmers harvested roughly twice as much grain as their neighbours during the 2022 drought. Yet the pilot did not include storage training, and many families sold their surplus at low prices immediately after harvest. Local extension services have never had the staff to follow up with farmers beyond the first planting season. This proposal seeks to scale the approach to 6,000 households across five districts.

passages.source_passage: Since January 2022, the Puertas Abiertas Scholarship Fund has supported 340 girls to attend lower and upper secondary schools in the highland municipality of San Ilario. At the mid-term point, retention among scholars stands at 91 percent, compared with 63 percent for girls in the same schools who did not receive support. Mentoring circles held every two weeks were valued highly by scholars and their mothers. The programme did not, however, reach girls in the three most remote villages, where no secondary school operates within walking distance. Transport stipends were introduced in the second year, but they weren't adjusted when fuel prices rose. Teachers noted that scholars participated more confidently in class and took on leadership roles in student councils.

passages.source_passage: The Ubuntu Lantern home-visiting programme in Mazeru District has enrolled 1,850 people living with HIV since its launch in July 2021. Trained caregivers conduct an average of four visits per client each month, checking adherence, wound care and nutrition. Viral suppression among enrolled clients rose from 72 percent to 86 percent over eighteen months. Clients described caregivers as trusted companions, and several said they would not have returned to the clinic without encouragement. Caregiver turnover remains a concern: 23 of the original 110 caregivers have left, mostly citing unpaid travel costs. The evaluation found no evidence that refresher training was delivered in the second year, and supervision checklists were not completed consistently.

passages.source_passage: In the twelve villages of Tessimor Ward, only 38 percent of households have access to an improved water source within thirty minutes' walk. Women and girls spend an estimated three hours each day collecting water from seasonal streams. A 2023 survey by the Clearwell Rural Foundation found that open defecation is practised by nearly half of households, and diarrhoeal disease accounts for one in five clinic visits among children under five. Four boreholes drilled by a previous project in 2016 are no longer functional, because no water committee was trained to maintain them. Communities have not been consulted on latrine designs in the past, which contributed to low uptake. The proposed project will drill eight new boreholes and support 900 households to build latrines.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 reporting year, the Stillwater Community Counselling Service provided 2,460 individual sessions to 615 clients across Brennock and its surrounding settlements. Lay counsellors supervised by clinical psychologists handled most first appointments. Seventy percent of clients completing at least six sessions showed reduced distress scores on the standard screening tool. Group sessions for bereaved parents were added in May and quickly reached capacity. We did not meet our target of training 40 lay counsellors, as only 28 completed the full certification course. Waiting times fell from five weeks to under two, thanks to the evening clinic funded by your grant. No client was turned away for inability to pay, and referrals from the district hospital doubled compared with the previous year.

passages.source_passage: Residents of the Kalvane informal settlements face frequent evictions, yet fewer than 15 percent have ever spoken to a lawyer. The nearest legal aid office is 42 kilometres away in the provincial capital and is open only three days a week. Since 2019, Justice Within Reach has trained community paralegals who mediate land disputes, accompany clients to court and help women claim inheritance rights. In 2023 alone, our 18 paralegals handled 1,140 cases, resolving most through mediation. Many disputes were not documented before our paralegals arrived, and local chiefs often didn't recognise written agreements. Demand now far exceeds capacity, and the service cannot expand into the eastern wards without additional funding.

passages.source_passage: In the 2023–24 school year, the Nourish Sahel Partnership served hot midday meals to 14,300 pupils in 52 primary schools across Dabouré Region. Average attendance in participating schools rose to 88 percent, compared with 74 percent before meals were introduced. Locally grown cowpeas and millet now make up 60 percent of the food basket, supporting more than 300 smallholder suppliers. Deliveries were disrupted for three weeks in February when the main road flooded, and some schools did not receive rice during that period. Kitchen staff in eleven schools still cook over open fires, as fuel-efficient stoves have not yet been installed. Head teachers report that pupils concentrate better in afternoon lessons.

passages.source_passage: The Sahaya Maternal Outreach Project operates in 27 villages of Rampura Block, linking pregnant women to the Chandpur primary health clinic. Since April 2022, outreach nurses have registered 1,620 pregnancies, and the share of women attending at least four antenatal visits has risen from 41 percent to 69 percent. Facility births increased steadily, though families in flood-prone hamlets still prefer home deliveries during the monsoon. The clinic did not have a functioning newborn resuscitation kit until October 2023. Community volunteers accompanied women to appointments and reminded mothers about postnatal checks. The evaluators found no reliable data on neonatal deaths, because village registers were not updated regularly.

passages.source_passage: Launched in 2021 by the Tidewatch Coastal Alliance, the early-warning programme covers 64 fishing communities along the Marenne coast. At mid-term, 48 communities have functioning siren towers and trained volunteer response teams. During Cyclone Ildra in November 2023, evacuation began nine hours before landfall, and no deaths were recorded in programme villages. SMS alerts reached about 80 percent of registered households, but older residents often did not own mobile phones. Evacuation drills were held twice a year in most communities. However, the evaluation found that shelters in the southern districts lacked water storage and were not accessible to people with disabilities.
